item.title: Excellent, Venerable Gotama! Excellent, Venerable Gotama! Just as one sets upright what was overturned, or reveals what was hidden, or shows the way to one…
item.description:
Excellent, Venerable Gotama! Excellent, Venerable Gotama! Just as one sets upright what was overturned, or reveals what was hidden, or shows the way to one who is lost, or holds up a lamp in the darkness so that those with eyes can see forms, so too, the Dhamma has been explained in many ways by Venerable Gotama. I go for refuge to Venerable Gotama, to the Dhamma, and to the Saṅgha. May Venerable Gotama accept me as a lay follower, from today until the end of my life, I take refuge.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 3.53

item.title: Bhikkhus, now I exhort you: 'All conditioned things are impermanent; strive on with diligence, do not be heedless.' This is the Tathāgata's last word.
item.description:
Bhikkhus, now I exhort you: 'All conditioned things are impermanent; strive on with diligence, do not be heedless.'
This is the Tathāgata's last word.

From: Dīgha Nikāya 16 – Mahāparinibbānasutta

item.title: Then the Venerable Vaṅgīsa, in the presence of the Blessed One, spoke these appropriate verses of praise: Whatever speech one utters, If it does not…
item.description:
Then the Venerable Vaṅgīsa, in the presence of the Blessed One, spoke these appropriate verses of praise:

Whatever speech one utters,
If it does not torment oneself,
Nor harm others,
That speech is well spoken.
One who speaks affectionate speech,
Speech that brings delight,
Speech that is not evil,
That speech is affectionate.
True speech is the deathless speech,
This is the ancient Dhamma,
The good person is said to be
Established in truth,
In meaning and in Dhamma,
Thus the wise say.
The word spoken by the Buddha,
Leading to the security of Nibbāna,
Making an end of all suffering,
That is the supreme speech.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 8.5

item.title: Whereas some samaṇas and brahmins, while enjoying food offered by the faithful, still live storing up and enjoying goods such as storing up food, storing…
item.description:
Whereas some samaṇas and brahmins, while enjoying food offered by the faithful, still live storing up and enjoying goods such as storing up food, storing up drinks, storing up cloth, storing up vehicles, storing up bedding, storing up perfumes, storing up delicacies — he abstains from storing up such goods. This is part of his virtue in terms of discipline.

From: Dīgha Nikāya 2 – Sāmaññaphalasutta

item.title: Bhikkhus, just as the awns of wheat or the awns of barley, when rightly directed, pressed by hand or foot, can pierce the hand or…
item.description:
Bhikkhus, just as the awns of wheat or the awns of barley, when rightly directed, pressed by hand or foot, can pierce the hand or foot or draw blood — this is possible. Why is that? Because the awns are rightly directed. So too, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu whose mind is rightly directed can pierce ignorance, arouse true knowledge, and realize Nibbāna — this is possible. Why is that? Because the mind is rightly directed.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 1.42

item.title: If a bhikkhu, bhikkhus, were to develop a mind of loving-kindness even for the duration of a finger-snap, that bhikkhu, bhikkhus, is called one who…
item.description:
If a bhikkhu, bhikkhus, were to develop a mind of loving-kindness even for the duration of a finger-snap, that bhikkhu, bhikkhus, is called one who dwells in jhāna without being empty, who acts upon the Teacher's instruction, who follows his advice, and who does not eat the country's almsfood in vain. How much more so those who make much of it!

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 1.53

item.title: Possessing seven qualities, bhikkhus, Sāriputta controls his mind and does not let the mind control him. What seven? Here, bhikkhus, Sāriputta is skilled in concentration,…
item.description:
Possessing seven qualities, bhikkhus, Sāriputta controls his mind and does not let the mind control him. What seven? Here, bhikkhus, Sāriputta is skilled in concentration, skilled in attaining concentration, skilled in abiding in concentration, skilled in emerging from concentration, skilled in the comfort of concentration, skilled in the range of concentration, and skilled in inducing concentration. Possessing these seven qualities, bhikkhus, Sāriputta controls his mind and does not let the mind control him.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 7.41

item.title: Having approached, that devata spoke these verses to the Venerable Nāgadatta: Nāgadatta, Enter the village at the proper time, And when you return from the…
item.description:
Having approached, that devata spoke these verses to the Venerable Nāgadatta:

Nāgadatta,
Enter the village at the proper time,
And when you return from the village,
Return early.
You live too involved
With laypeople,
Overcome by too many
Feelings of pain and pleasure.
I fear that Nāgadatta,
This reckless one,
Will be bound and fettered
By household affairs.
Do not fall into
The power of Death,
How can one escape
Māra's control?

The Venerable Nāgadatta, stirred by that devata, was greatly moved.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 9.7

item.title: - Bhikkhus, if wanderers of other sects should ask you: 'In what abiding, friends, does Samaṇa Gotama dwell much during the rains?' Being asked thus,…
item.description:
- Bhikkhus, if wanderers of other sects should ask you: 'In what abiding, friends, does Samaṇa Gotama dwell much during the rains?' Being asked thus, bhikkhus, you should answer those wanderers: 'In the concentration of mindfulness of breathing, friends, the Blessed One dwells much during the rains.' Here, bhikkhus, mindful I breathe in, mindful I breathe out. Or breathing in long, I understand: 'I breathe in long'; or breathing out long, I understand: 'I breathe out long'; or breathing in short, I understand: 'I breathe in short'; or breathing out short, I understand: 'I breathe out short' ... 'Contemplating relinquishment, I breathe in,' I understand thus; 'Contemplating relinquishment, I breathe out,' I understand thus. Bhikkhus, one speaking rightly, if he were to say 'This is a noble abiding, this is a Brahmā abiding, this is the Tathāgata's abiding,' should say that the concentration of mindfulness of breathing is a noble abiding, a Brahmā abiding, the Tathāgata's abiding.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 54.11

item.title: How, householder, is one who wanders without abode? The bondage of dwelling on the sign of form, householder, has been abandoned by the Tathāgata, cut…
item.description:
How, householder, is one who wanders without abode? The bondage of dwelling on the sign of form, householder, has been abandoned by the Tathāgata, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, made not to arise again, not to be born in the future. Therefore, the Tathāgata is called one who wanders without abode. The bondage of dwelling on the sign of sound... sign of odor... sign of taste... sign of touch... sign of mental object, householder, has been abandoned by the Tathāgata, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, made not to arise again, not to be born in the future. Therefore, the Tathāgata is called one who wanders without abode. Thus, householder, is one who wanders without abode.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 22.3
